summary: Phase 149O.20L.3 -- Full-HBDC Production Readiness Integration. Production-integration phase: implements HMRC-001 v1.1's independently-verified eighth PREPARED readiness prerequisite (HMRC-REQ-086-100, Section 19A) in live production, exactly as specified, trusting the independently-verified 149O.20L.1/149O.20L.2 contract text but re-deriving every implementation obligation directly from the current HMRC-001 v1.1 source (Section 19A read in full before any edit). Added class_b_conformance_status_satisfies_readiness -- a pure, deterministic, total, closed-enum mapping helper (status is ClassBConformanceStatus.COMPLIANT, mirroring certification_status_satisfies_readiness's exact-identity precedent; no string comparison, no truthiness, no negative membership list; verified by AST inspection to contain exactly one Compare node using ast.Is) -- and a new class_b_deployment_conformance_satisfies_readiness HATPMandatoryActivationReadinessCheck, appended to the existing checks list inside the single production readiness-assembly function (_assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness_at_root), the sole such function in the module (confirmed by AST walk: no other function anywhere in hatp_mandatory_cutover.py constructs HATPMandatoryActivationReadinessCheck instances). Because assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness and _write_cutover_transition's lock-held readiness_check callback both call this same function unmodified, both the advisory path and the authoritative lock-held re-check automatically observe the eighth term -- no duplicate wiring, no second lock, no parallel gate. The eighth term calls the canonical verify_class_b_deployment_conformance() (hatp_class_b_conformance.py) fresh on every single assessment invocation -- no cache, no module-global, no lazy reuse -- and fails closed (satisfied=False) on any raised exception, non-ClassBConformanceStatus value, or any current/future enum member other than COMPLIANT, while preserving the exact observed status string in the check's detail field rather than collapsing it to an undifferentiated Boolean (HMRC-REQ-090). All seven pre-existing checks are byte-for-byte unmodified (independently reconstructed from the true phase-entry commit 5e9d72d3 and diffed against the current source: identical names, identical construction logic, only one net addition). The eight-term vector is joined by the pre-existing ready = len(unmet_reasons) == 0 conjunction, unmodified: Class-B COMPLIANT together with any other unmet term still yields ready=False, and every other term satisfied together with Class-B not COMPLIANT still yields ready=False -- no ready-via-Class-B-alone path exists or was added (HMRC-REQ-096). No production signature (assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness, _assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness_at_root, activate_hatp_mandatory, _activate_hatp_mandatory_at_root) accepts a class_b_ok/class_b_status/skip_class_b-shaped override parameter -- independently confirmed by inspect.signature() across all four (HMRC-REQ-095); test seams may monkeypatch the verifier itself, never bypass via a parameter. Production diff scope is exactly one file: src/pcae/core/hatp_mandatory_cutover.py, +51/-0, wholly additive (two new imports, one new helper function, one new check block inserted between the existing seventh check and the unmet_reasons computation). All three Class-B verifier modules, hatp_mandatory_certification.py, and HMRC-001/HMIC-001/HBDC-001 are confirmed byte-identical to the true phase-entry commit 5e9d72d3 by direct git show comparison. A new, dedicated 61-test focused module (tests/test_phase_149o_20l_3_full_hbdc_production_readiness_integration.py) covers: exact seven-term baseline reconstruction from the phase-entry commit and the exact eight-term current vector with a precise +1 delta; full closed-enum mapping across all six live ClassBConformanceStatus members plus non-member/malformed-input fail-closed cases; evidence/Boolean-separation diagnostics for every status; the full conjunction truth table (all-eight-true, Class-B-alone-false, one-old-check-false-with-Class-B-true, Class-B-INDETERMINATE); per-assessment freshness (a call-counting monkeypatch proves one call per assessment, no memoization, and at least two independent calls across an advisory-plus-lock-held-recheck sequence); advisory-path and lock-held-recheck inclusion of the eighth term; a TOCTOU test in which an advisory pre-lock read observes COMPLIANT but the verifier flips to NON_COMPLIANT before the lock-held re-check, which correctly blocks the write and produces no Cutover Record; verifier-exception fail-closed behavior; no-caller-override signature checks across all four entrypoints; single-constructor-site and single-caller AST checks; read-only-assessment (no protected-root creation) confirmation; and the full byte-identity/CBV-S1/B-149O.20L.1-1 regression suite. All 61 pass standalone. A real, completely unmocked call to assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness on this genuinely unprovisioned host returns exactly eight checks, with the Class-B term unsatisfied (verify_class_b_deployment_conformance independently confirmed to return NON_COMPLIANT on this host) and ready=False overall; the repository was confirmed clean (no side effect) immediately after every such real-host call. Six pre-existing current-production test files (never historical-pinned ones -- each verified individually against the true phase-entry commit, pre-edit, to distinguish transient-dirty-tree artifacts from genuine causation) required updates because their live assertions about the seven-term vector, the six-item HMRC-REQ-054 conjunction, or the one-hop/transitive pcae.* import closure of the strict HMIC-bound subset were now stale: test_phase_149o_19_5f_hmic_activation_readiness_integration.py and test_phase_149o_19_5g_hmic_assembled_attack_matrix_hardening.py (added a class_b_compliant fixture parameter, default True, to their existing _assess() helpers and direct-call test bodies, mirroring their own existing operational_substrate parameter pattern; updated two live seven-to-eight check-count assertions), test_phase_149o_19_hmrc_mandatory_consumption_independent_verification.py (added the eighth name to one live set-equality assertion), and test_phase_149o_19_3_hmic_contract_independent_verification.py plus test_phase_149o_19_3r_1_hmic_frozen_identity_repair_independent_reverification.py (added the two new Class-B verifier imports, plus their own transitive hatp_environment_lock_verifier.py dependency, to each file's existing documented-unbound-dependency allowlist, with a full rationale paragraph mirroring the existing hatp_mandatory_certification precedent already in both files -- these are genuinely new, additive, documented exceptions, mirroring CBV-S1's own established precedent that the Class-B verifier modules are deliberately outside HMIC-REQ-050's frozen scope, not a repair of an existing gap). None of these six files' historical-pinned assertions (fixed-commit byte-identity checks, requirement-ID gaplessness checks, or similar) were touched. Separately, 21 tests across 8 prior-phase modules (149O.20F, 149O.20G, 149O.20K.2, 149O.20K.3, 149O.20L.1, 149O.20L.1A, 149O.20L.1B, 149O.20L class_b analysis) now fail as an expected, individually-attributed, permanent consequence of this phase's own authorized wiring -- each asserted a form of "not yet wired into production / exactly seven terms / zero consumers of the verifier outside its own module" that was true as of that phase's own conclusion and is, by design, no longer true; these were left untouched, per the phase's own "historical snapshot tests should remain historical" instruction, and are not weakened or deleted. HMRC-001 remains v1.1, unchanged. CBV-S1 and B-149O.20L.1-1 remain unchanged, independently reconfirmed closed.
